messages:
miguel: Hey support — customer acct_9b2f seeing a burst of 429s around 2026-03-17T09:34:00Z despite Console quota panel showing ~20k tokens available. Sample req id: req_20260317_9a7. They say it was a short spike, then full throttle for ~90s. Screenshot attached.

amy: Thanks Miguel — I can take this. Can you paste the raw request IDs and approximate UTC window? I'll pull enforcer logs and quota snapshots.

miguel: pasted IDs: req_20260317_9a7, req_20260317_9b1, req_20260317_9c3. Window 09:33:50–09:35:30Z. Customer says they retried once and then succeeded at 09:36:20Z.

amy: Pulling edge/enforcer logs now. I see 429 responses with body: {"code":"RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED","reason":"enforcer::token_bucket_check_failed"} between 09:34:01–09:35:40Z. Quota service shows no enforcement events for acct_9b2f in that same minute. Escalating to eng-infra.

sam: on it. I pulled the enforcer instance logs and the redis client logs. Quick snapshot: around 09:34:03Z there are repeated redis GET/INCR timeouts against tokens:acct_9b2f:bucket followed by enforcer returning 429. Looks like the enforcer treats redis read timeouts as fail-closed for safety.

sam: redis INFO (sanitized):
# Server
redis_version:6.2.8
used_memory:1042345600
used_memory_peak:1290341120
maxmemory:1073741824
maxmemory_policy:volatile-lru
# Stats
expired_keys:0
evicted_keys:2381
instantaneous_ops_per_sec:4200

sam: Key-level check: the token key for acct_9b2f was present at 09:33:58Z then missing at 09:34:02Z (evicted). Redis returned \"nil\" on GET. Enforcer code path treats missing key + failed INCR as quota unavailable and responds 429.

lee: telemetry here — the Console quota panel is powered by the aggregated usage feed (kafka -> aggregator -> OLAP). That pipeline saw the customer's tokens up to 09:33:59Z and then ingested nothing for the next 30s because the enforcer rejected traffic (so pipeline didn't emit successful-consumption events). The dashboard shows the last known snapshot (full tokens) until the next snapshot rollup (~15s), so it looked like tokens were available. Essentially two different truth sources: live token state in Redis vs periodic snapshots in OLAP.

sam: Root cause hypothesis: Redis evictions (memory pressure) removed live token buckets for some customers; enforcer's current behavior treats missing/timeout as fail-closed, causing 429s. Dashboard shows stale snapshot which still indicated tokens available.

amy: That explains the discrepancy we reported — good find. Any immediate mitigation we can apply so customer isn't blocked?

sam: Short term: I can put acct_9b2f on the temporary allowlist to bypass token checks. Also increasing redis maxmemory and spinning up additional shard to reduce evictions. I pushed a small config bump to the redis cluster (maxmemory -> 1.5GB) and added a replica. Deploy-bot: can you confirm recent redis config change?

deploy-bot: cluster-config-updater deployed redis/maxmemory=1610612736 to prod-redis-cluster-3 at 2026-03-17T09:45:12Z (canary 10%).

sam: After the config bump, evicted_keys count stopped incrementing and the enforcer no longer hit redis timeouts for the sample account. I also added a temporary rule to treat transient redis timeouts as fail-open for non-enterprise plans (canaryed).

lee: Telemetry note: adding metric enforcer.redis_read_errors and redis.evictions and wiring them to paging. Also adding an advisory in Console that shows live_enforcer_status vs snapshot_staleness so Support can see divergence.

amy: Miguel — I whitelisted acct_9b2f and asked infra to scale redis. Can you have the customer retry and confirm they no longer see 429s?

miguel: Customer retried at 09:51:05Z and got success. They confirmed no more 429s for the following 10 minutes.

amy: Closing loop with customer, logging RCA. Proposed long-term fixes: 1) prevent Redis OOMs (increase memory + better eviction policy), 2) change enforcer to use a safe fail-open policy for short redis timeouts (with rate limits), 3) emit and page on redis_evictions and enforcer_redis_errors, 4) surface live vs snapshot staleness in Console.

sam: I'll open tickets for infra and enforcer workitems and include the sample req ids and redis-key traces.

amy: Thanks all — summarizing for support ticket: cause = Redis eviction + enforcer fail-closed behavior; symptom = 429s while Console showed tokens because Console used slightly older snapshots; mitigation = temporary whitelist + redis scale + canary fallback; next steps = infra + enforcer fixes + telemetry alerts.

miguel: customer happy, closing. :white_check_mark:
